title: Reverse a String In Place
statement:
Reverse a C string **in place** -- modify the caller's buffer rather
than allocating a new one.

## Your function

```
void reverse_string(char *s);
```

After it returns, `s` holds the same characters in the opposite order
and is still terminated by `'\0'`.

## Watch out

- The empty string is valid input. So is a single character.
- Do not move the terminator. `strlen` still has to work afterwards.
- Swapping from both ends towards the middle needs only one pass and
  no extra memory.

tests.name: empty string
tests.description: Nothing to do -- but make sure you do not read or write past the terminator.
